config.title: Testing Express apps

intro.title: Testing Express apps
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Express API and learn how to test it using the Jest testing framework and Supertest library. You will understand the core concept of automated testing, which helps ensure your application works correctly by writing code that verifies your endpoints return the expected responses. The main technologies involved are Express for the server, Jest as the test runner, and Supertest for making HTTP requests to your API in tests. By the end, you'll have a tested Express app that handles GET and POST requests, giving you confidence in your code's reliability.
intro.usecase: Testing Express apps is essential for ensuring reliability in production systems like e-commerce platforms, where payment processing and inventory management APIs must handle thousands of requests without errors. In SaaS applications, automated tests verify that user authentication, data retrieval endpoints, and subscription billing APIs function correctly across different user tiers. Developers use testing to validate API contracts before deployment, preventing broken integrations in mobile apps or third-party services that depend on these endpoints. This practice is critical for maintaining uptime in financial services dashboards, healthcare data portals, and real-time collaboration tools where API failures directly impact user experience and business operations.

objectives: Initialize a testing environment for Express applications using Jest and Supertest
Configure test suites to isolate Express route handlers from external dependencies
Implement unit tests for Express middleware functions with mocked request/response objects
Construct integration tests for Express routes that simulate HTTP requests and validate responses
Manipulate test data to verify error handling and edge cases in Express endpoints
Apply test-driven development principles by writing tests before implementing route functionality
Integrate testing scripts into the Express project's package.json for automated test execution

steps.title: Import required testing modules
steps.instruction: Import the required testing modules: supertest for HTTP testing and jest for test framework.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import both supertest and jest. You'll need to import them as separate statements.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have both supertest and jest imported and ready to use for testing your Express app.
successCriteria: supertest and jest are both imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you import both supertest and jest. Check that you have both require() statements.
steps.feedbackWrong: import both supertest and jest using require() statements. Remember: supertest is for HTTP testing, jest is the test framework.

steps.title: Create a basic Express app for testing
steps.instruction: Create a basic Express application with a simple GET endpoint that returns a JSON response with a message property set to 'Hello, world!'.
steps.hint: Initialize an Express app, define a GET route at the root path ('/'), and send a JSON response with the message.
steps.expectedOutcome: An Express app is created with a GET endpoint at '/' that returns a JSON object with a message property.
successCriteria: The Express app is created and exports the app instance, with a GET route at '/' that sends a JSON response containing a message property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've created an Express app instance, defined a GET route at '/', and are sending a JSON response with a message property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The app wasn't created correctly. Ensure you're using Express to create an app instance, defining a GET route at '/', and sending a JSON response with a message property.

steps.title: Export the Express app for testing
steps.instruction: Export the Express app instance so it can be imported in test files. Add an export statement for your app.
steps.hint: Use module.exports to make your app available to other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your Express app will be exported and ready to be imported in test files.
successCriteria: The Express app instance is exported using module.exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're exporting the app instance correctly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The app isn't exported yet. Use module.exports to export your Express app.

steps.title: Create a test file structure
steps.instruction: Create a test file named 'app.test.js' and import the Express app and supertest's request function.
steps.hint: Create a new file with the .test.js extension. Use require() to import both your app and supertest's request function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test file named 'app.test.js' is created with imports for the app and supertest's request function.
successCriteria: The test file imports the Express app using require('./app') and imports supertest's request function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both the Express app and supertest's request function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test file structure isn't quite right. Remember to create a test file and import both the app and supertest.

steps.title: Write a basic GET endpoint test
steps.instruction: Write a test that checks if the GET endpoint returns status 200. Use the describe and it blocks to structure your test.
steps.hint: Inside the describe block, use it to define a test case that sends a GET request to the endpoint and expects a 200 status code.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test case is written that sends a GET request to the endpoint and expects a 200 status code.
successCriteria: The test includes a describe block, an it block, uses request to send a GET request, and expects a 200 status code.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your test includes a describe block, an it block, uses request to send a GET request, and expects a 200 status code.
steps.feedbackWrong: Your test is missing key components. Review the example and ensure you have a describe block, an it block, a GET request using request, and an expectation for status 200.

steps.title: Add response body validation to the test
steps.instruction: Inside the existing test, add an assertion to verify the response body contains the expected JSON data.
steps.hint: Use the expect() function to check the response body property. The response object from supertest has a .body property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The test now validates both the status code and the response body content.
successCriteria: The test includes an expect() statement that checks the response.body matches expected data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to add an expect() statement for the response.body.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding an assertion like expect(response.body).toEqual({ message: 'Example response' }) inside the test.

steps.title: Create a POST endpoint test
steps.instruction: Add a new describe block for testing a POST endpoint that sends JSON data and checks the response status and body.
steps.hint: Create a new describe block with a descriptive name for the POST endpoint, then add an it block inside it to test the POST request.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new describe block for POST endpoint testing is added to the test file structure.
successCriteria: A describe block with a name for the POST endpoint is created, containing an it block for testing the POST request.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a describe block, but make sure it contains an it block for the POST test.
steps.feedbackWrong: The POST endpoint test structure is missing. Add a describe block with a name for the POST endpoint and an it block inside it.

steps.title: Add error handling test
steps.instruction: Create a new describe block for testing error handling on an invalid route, such as GET /nonexistent, that verifies it returns a 404 status code.
steps.hint: Add a new describe block after your existing POST endpoint test. Inside it, write an it block that uses request(app).get('/nonexistent') and expects a 404 status.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new describe block for testing error handling is added, with an it block that checks for a 404 status on an invalid route.
successCriteria: A describe block for error handling is created with an it block that uses request(app).get('/nonexistent') and expects status 404.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your describe block includes an it block that specifically tests a non-existent route and expects a 404 status.
steps.feedbackWrong: The error handling test is missing or incorrect. Ensure you add a describe block with an it block that tests an invalid route and checks for a 404 status code.

steps.title: Set up test environment configuration
steps.instruction: Add a Jest configuration comment at the top of your test file to set up the test environment for Express.
steps.hint: Add a comment line that mentions Jest configuration for testing Express apps.
steps.analogousExample: // Jest configuration for testing Express apps
steps.expectedOutcome: Your test file will have a Jest configuration comment at the top to properly set up the test environment.
successCriteria: A comment about Jest configuration for Express testing is added at the top of the test file.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a comment, but make sure it mentions Jest configuration for Express testing.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Jest configuration comment for Express testing is missing or incorrect.

steps.title: Run the tests and verify results
steps.instruction: Run the test suite using the npm test command and verify that all tests pass successfully.
steps.hint: Open your terminal in the project directory and execute the test command. Check the output for any failures.
steps.analogousExample:
// Running tests in a Node.js project
npm test
steps.expectedOutcome: The test suite executes and shows all tests passing with green checkmarks.
successCriteria: All tests pass successfully with no failures reported.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: Some tests are failing. Review the error messages to identify issues in your endpoints or test logic.
steps.feedbackWrong: Tests are not running. Ensure you have the correct test command and that your test file is properly configured.
